The refusal case (labels verbatim in harness/idempotency/test.sh): "the reused key under a different payload is refused, typed" and "409, typed, before a second execution" - confirmed live, alongside "replay answered duplicate" for the happy path.

harness/idempotency/adapters/dryrun.py docstring: "which is the adapter-today row PASS.md B3 records for this element" naming (F-b3-16) "key on the wire, no lease", and "none. The conformance run's race case proves the gap: without a lock around" a claim-then-write. harness/idempotency/test.sh section 3 ("deliberate breakage: remove the lease acquisition, leave the key on the wire") measures the concurrent outcome live: "every concurrent copy won: executions=20, overlapped=0", "7/8: only the race case fails".
note: What happens: with no lease, all 20 concurrent presenters of the same key each observe "not found" and each execute - double execution under concurrency, not merely a slow duplicate answer. What is given up: atomic claim-before-execute. What is preserved: post-hoc duplicate detection once the log is folded. The second, lease-based adapter (E-swap-candidate-any-keyed-lease-store) closes this: conformance.py asserts overlapped >= 1 answered in_flight rather than executed twice.

evidence: harness/idempotency/adapters/second.py docstring: "Different execution model from the fold: claim() takes a real compare-and-set" under a lock before execution begins, holding an in-flight state, so "a duplicate arriving while the winner is still working is answered mid-flight (in_flight=True), which the fold can never do."
falsifier: If swapping to the lease adapter required conformance.py to add a special-cased branch for it, rather than just running the identical case suite by configuration, the interface would be shaped around the fold adapter.
note: Confirmed live: "3 axes differ (conditionality, in-flight support, overlap observed)" and 8/8 cases pass on both adapters (harness/idempotency/test.sh section 2).
